test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct about Gupta emperor, Samudragupta?

a) He was the successor of Chandragupta I.

b) His court poet Bhimsena composed a prashasti of praise for him which was known as Gwalior Prashasti.

c) On his gold coins he was depicted playing the harp which shows his passion for music.

d) He held the title of Ashvamedha Parakram.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Statement b only__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Samudragupta:**

__
 
• The **first prominent king** of the Gupta Dynasty was **Samudragupta.**
 
• He is Known as the **Napoleon of India for his conquests.**
 
• **Samudragupta's court poet and minister 'Harisena' composed the Allahabad pillar Inscription or Prayag Prasasti.**
 
• The **Pillar was an Ashokan Pillar erected by Ashoka **six centuries before him.
 
• This** inscription serves as a praise for Samudragupta and mentions both his conquests and the boundaries of the Gupta Empire.**
 
• As per this inscription,** Samudragupta defeated 9 kings in the North, 12 Kings in the South, reduced all the Atavika states to vassalage.**
 
• **Samudragupta was defeated, captured, and later released by the kings of Palakkad, Kottura, and Avamukta.**
 
• Samudragupta used a **variety of tactics, including violent devastation.**
 
• **He made the kings of the forest states in central India his servants.**
 
• The **Shaka-Murundas are included among the monarchs **who made an effort to appease **Chandragupta in his father Samudragupta's Allahabad Pillar inscription.**
 
• The Allahabad Pillar inscription mentions that the **Kushana rulers of North-West India and the Saka satraps of western India** also submitted to him.
 
• **The Kushan ruler by name of Shahanushahi** is said to have **personally appeared before Samudra Gupta and tendered voluntary submission** and **agreed to accept and circulate the imperial coins as currency** in his territories and **offered his daughter in marriage to the emperor.**
 
• The **empire of Samudra Gupta probably extended from Afghanistan in the west to Assam in the east and from Nepal in the north to Kanchi in the south**.
 
• To commemorate his victories he performed** Ashvamedha Yaga and donated liberally to Brahmins, the poor, and the needy.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Gupta dynasty was established by Shrigupta.** He hailed from either Magadha (Bihar) or Prayag (eastern U.P.).
 
• His son **Ghatotkacha, who carried the title of maharaja**, appears to be some small king about whom nothing much is known.

 
 

 **Chandragupta-I**
 
 
 
• The **real founder of the Gupta empire was Chandragupta I (AD 319–334).**
 
• The year of his accession in A.D. **319 marks the beginning of the Gupta era.**
 
• He took the title of **maharajadhiraja (king of kings)**.
 
• He **married a Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi.**
 
 
• This **event is recorded** in a **series of gold coins issued by Chandragupta.**
 
 
 
• Chandragupta, was ruling over Magadha (Bihar) Saket (modern Ayodhya) and Prayaga (modern Allahabad) with his capital at Pataliputra (Modern Patna).
 
 
 
 

 **Samudragupta**
 
 
 
• Chandragupta was succeeded by his **son Samudragupta (A.D. 335-375).**
 
 
 
 

 **Chandragupta II**
 
 
 
• Samudragupta was succeeded by his** son Chandragupta II (AD 375–414)** also known as **Chandragupta Vikramaditya**, he not only extended his father’s empire but also consolidated his position through matrimonial alliances with other royal dynasties of the period.
 
• **He married Kuvernaga, the Naga princess and had a daughter Prabhavati from her.**
 
• **Prabhavati was given in marriage to Rudrasena II of the Vakataka dynasty ruling in Deccan.**
 
 
• After the death of her husband, **Prabhavati ruled the territory as regent to her minor son with the help of her father.**
 
 
 
• The control of Vakataka territory proved very beneficial to Chandragupta II, as he was now able to target his other enemies better.
 
• His **greatest military achievement was his victory over the Shaka kings** and assumed the **tilte of Sakari (Destroyer of Sakas).**
 
• This conquest made Gupta empire reach up to the western coast.
 
• An **iron pillar inscription at Mehrauli in Delhi indicates that his empire included even north-western India and Bengal.**
 
• He took the **title of Vikramaditya** i.e. the **one who is as powerful as the sun.**
 
• Chandragupta II is remembered for his **patronage of art and literature.**
 
• He is credited with maintaining **nine luminaries (navaratna)** in his court.
 
 
• The great **Sanskrit poet **and **playwright Kalidasa was the most notable of them all.**
 
 
 
• The **Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa Hien (AD 404–411)** visited India during his reign.
 
• He has left an account of the life of people in India in the fifth century AD.
 
 
 
 

 **Kumaragupta**
 
 
 
• He reigned from **AD 415 to AD 455.**
 
• He inherited the vast empire of his father Chandragupta II.
 
• He was a powerful ruler who ruled for 40 years defending his kingdom.
 
• He adopted the title of **Mahendraditya.**
 
• He** founded the Nalanda University** (a renowned university of ancient India).
 
• **Kalidas (the Shakespeare of India) flourished during the reign of both Chandragupta II and Kumaragupta I.**
 
• He was the** worshipper of Lord Kartikeya (son of Lord Shiva, his vehicle is peacock).**
 
• He **died during the war with the Hunas.**
 
 
 
 

 **Skandagupta**
 
 
 
• **Skandagupta is known as ''Vikramaditya'' Saviour of India as he successfully fought the battle against the invading Huns.**
 
• He ascended the throne in **455 AD and ruled till 467 AD.**
 
• Skandagupta **issued five types of gold coins:**
 
 
• **Archer type, King and queen type, Chhatra type, Lion-slayer type and Horseman type.**
 
 
 
• His **silver coins are of four types**:
 
 
• **Garuda type, Bull type, Altar type and Madhyadesha type**.
